text:
Sam: quick RFC follow-up — proposal to use sealed manifests + a tiny verifier sidecar for disconnected installs. goal: make upgrades atomic on-device without requiring a full-on operator, and keep rollback cheap.

Jia: sounds promising. how do you mean "sealed" here? immutable manifest with per-component activation markers? :thinking:

Sam: exactly — manifest is content-addressed, signed by build pipeline. we include an activation plan that is just a list of components + activation tokens. validator verifies signatures and checks local preconditions.

Omar: a couple quick concerns: 1) operatorless means how do we handle partial failures (power loss mid-activate)? 2) how do we avoid replaying old activations?

Sam: good Q. answers: 1) activation is two-phase: stage -> verify -> atomic handoff (rename/overlay swap). on power loss we detect incomplete handoff and roll back using staged marker. 2) tokens include monotonic epoch + manifest hash; verifier enforces epoch monotonicity.

Carol: can we avoid a global monotonic counter? some sites won't want extra state. maybe use per-node sequence with signed monotonic nonces from the build service when preparing sealed bundles?

Sam: we considered that. approach: bundle includes a monotonic 'activation_id' signed by the builder. verifier stores last seen activation_id locally. no external call needed at activation time.

Maya: what about delta bundles vs full image? if we allow tiny deltas we need to ensure activation ordering still prevents missing deps.

Sam: deltas are allowed but manifest expresses dependency graph + preconditions. verifier rejects an activation if required blobs are missing. delta application happens in the stage phase.

Omar: how do we handle signature verification keys and rotation? KMS calls are out for air-gapped installs.

Sam: plan: include signer public keys in an "operator root.json" that's part of the seed bundle. support an offline key rotation process: new root signed by old key + proof-of-operator (manual step). document a recovery flow for lost keys.

Jia: can you paste a tiny example of the activation flow?

Sam: sure:
```
# stage
verifier stage --bundle /mnt/usb/bundle.tar.gz --out /var/lib/staged/234
# verify signatures + preconds
verifier verify /var/lib/staged/234
# atomic activate (rename mount or swap symlink)
verifier activate /var/lib/staged/234
```

Carol: I like the swap symlink approach for minimal downtime. assume we need a safety timeout for long-running migrations; activation should be reversible until the timeout.

Sam: agreed — activation atomically flips symlink and writes an activation record with a TTL window (default 5m) during which operator can trigger revert. after TTL, we mark activation complete.

Maya: tests? we should add a harness that simulates power loss, partial blob availability, and key rotation. also add chaos tests for the symlink swap.

Sam: yep plan is unit + e2e harness that runs locally and in CI for connected builds, and an "offline" test runner for air-gapped acceptance.

DeployBot: deployment note: image builder will start emitting sealed bundles with activation_id v0.2 starting next week. will announce when rolling out. :rocket:

Omar: one last thought — operatorless is great for simple sites, but we should design the sidecar API so an operator can still orchestrate upgrades when available. thin RPC surface: stage/verify/activate/list/status.

Sam: that's the intention. sidecar exposes a local unix socket and simple JSON RPC so an operator can call the same verbs.

Jia: +1. seems fairly bounded. can you split this into an RFC doc with sections: activation protocol, state machine, key rotation, test plan, compatibility matrix? I'll review tomorrow.

Sam: will do. filing RFC now and will assign owners for tests. thanks all. :thumbsup:
